findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 2
Raise: Functional. Case: normal use - An HTML design draft contains an inline script with `button.className = 'transition-opacity'; // replaced transition-all`. Line 39 skips HTML, so `motion-all` still reads the JavaScript comment and refuses the clean draft; `src/forge/design.py:129-133` shows that Forge checks these HTML files during plan read. A trailing JavaScript waiver inside the script is ignored for the same reason. JSX and TSX also remain affected when a label has an apostrophe and the comment quotes the old class: in `const C = () => <button className="transition-opacity">Don't</button>; // replaced 'transition-all'`, the quoted-string matcher consumes the `//` marker and leaves the comment visible. The synchronized `.forge/design/ui-checks.js:39` has the same behavior.
findings.title: Strip trailing JavaScript comments before applying motion-all
